grading_basis: Use unchanged benchmark-v4 questions and material facts. Correct requires all material requested facts, accepting semantic equivalents and explicit local corrections; Partial means an omission or unresolved material fact without contradiction; Incorrect requires a material contradictory operative ruling. Assess whole answers and their own explanatory content independently of support labels; do not import other answers.

decisions.reason: The introductory one-cube clause incorrectly adds even if cured, but the immediately following clause expressly replaces that instruction for a cured color: the action instead removes all cubes of that color. Read as a whole, this explicit instead clause supplies the operative conditional exception rather than leaving two alternative treatment rules. Together with one action per different color and return to supply, the answer resolves all requested facts. The final caveat requests no extra procedure beyond that correctly stated per-color treatment. This is consistent with evaluating the complete conditional rule in seed-iteration-04, while acknowledging the inaccurate lead-in rather than ignoring it.

Correctly states three cubes, no outbreak for reaching three in the stipulated initially empty city, and discard to the Infection Discard Pile before Intensify. The further statement that a city already at three outbreaks when another cube is required is a true sufficient trigger; it does not say this is the only Epidemic trigger. In this zero-cube context, the reaching-three statement addresses the named empty-city case rather than denying an outbreak for a previously nonempty city. The same entry's evidence expressly preserves the nonempty-city fill-to-three-then-outbreak rule. No material contradictory ruling is added.

Supplies all three fixed material facts for the named zero-cube city: place three, no outbreak merely from that placement reaching three, and Infection Discard Pile before Intensify. Its already-three/fourth-cube conditional is sufficient, not an only-if restriction on all Epidemic outbreaks. It makes no claim that a one- or two-cube Epidemic city avoids an outbreak; its own evidence explicitly states the existing-cubes exception. Thus it does not contradict that exception or the requested empty-city ruling.

Supplies immediate four-cure victory regardless of cubes or eradication, eighth-outbreak loss, failure to place actually required cubes of the needed color during epidemic/outbreak/infection, and failure to draw two Player cards after actions. The formulation that they lose if they cannot place required cubes during those resolutions states failed required placement itself as the loss trigger, rather than reserve depletion or a later checkpoint. That is a semantic statement of loss at the failed placement; the exact adverb immediate is not required to repeat it. No other answer or evidence clause is imported to supply timing.

Gives all other setup facts but does not say disease cubes are separated by color. Nearby disease cubes do not establish color separation, and its evidence also only names board/supplies. The unchanged key explicitly includes separating the cube supplies by color, so this is an omitted material setup detail without contradiction.

Correctly identifies counted Player cards, excluded Role/Reference cards and stored Planner Event, and discarding or playing Events until at most seven. It omits the fixed material timing clause to resolve any drawn Epidemics first. The caveat about no priority between discard and Event play does not answer Epidemic priority. Do not borrow Q14 or timing from another entry. No contrary timing asserted.
